t: The Solatium Scheme, 1989 for hit-and-run victims was replaced in 2022 by:
o: Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022
e: The 2022 Scheme notified under Section 161 enhanced compensation to ₹2 lakh for death and ₹50,000 for grievous hurt and streamlined the claim process through the district-level Claims Enquiry Officer and Claims Settlement Commissioner.

t: Who among the following has an insurable interest in a car purchased under a hire-purchase agreement?
o: Both the hirer and the financier
Neither, until the final instalment is paid
e: The hirer, as owner in possession under Section 2(30), bears the risk of loss and legal liability, while the financier has a financial interest in the vehicle; the hire-purchase endorsement protects the financier's interest in claim proceeds.

t: The India Motor Tariff that remained in force until de-tariffing was the edition effective from:
e: The India Motor Tariff 2002 took effect on 1 July 2002; its wordings, endorsements (IMTs) and general regulations continue to be used by insurers even after pricing was de-tariffed in 2007.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 66 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which of the following requires a permit to ply in a public place?
o: A two-wheeler used by the owner
e: Section 66 mandates a permit for transport vehicles (goods and passenger carriers), with some exemptions. Use of a transport vehicle without a valid permit is a breach that can affect claims.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 56 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a certificate of fitness is compulsory for:
e: A transport vehicle is not deemed validly registered unless it carries a valid certificate of fitness. Private vehicles are not subject to this requirement.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 166(4) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Claims Tribunal shall treat which document as an application for compensation?
o: The FIR filed by the victim
The accident information report forwarded by the police under Section 159
e: The police report under Section 159 (detailed accident report) is deemed to be an application for compensation, enabling the Tribunal to proceed even if the victim's family has not filed a claim.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (inserted in 2019), where an offence is committed by a juvenile driving a vehicle:
o: Only the juvenile is punished under the Juvenile Justice Act
The insurer is liable to pay the fine
The guardian or owner of the vehicle is deemed guilty unless he proves the offence was committed without his knowledge or he exercised due diligence
e: Section 199A makes the guardian or vehicle owner liable (fine up to ₹25,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years) and provides for cancellation of the vehicle's registration, unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 174 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, where a person fails to pay the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, the amount may be recovered:
o: Only by filing a civil suit
As arrears of land revenue through the Collector
e: Section 174 allows the Tribunal to issue a certificate to the Collector, who recovers the award amount as arrears of land revenue, giving awards a quick enforcement mechanism.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: In Bajaj Allianz General Insurance v. Rambha Devi (Constitution Bench, 2024), the Supreme Court affirmed that:
o: A holder of a licence for 'light motor vehicle' can drive a transport vehicle of that class with gross vehicle weight up to 7,500 kg without a separate transport endorsement
An LMV licence does not permit driving any transport vehicle
Transport vehicles require a licence only above 12,000 kg
Insurers may repudiate all claims involving transport vehicles driven on LMV licences
e: The Constitution Bench upheld Mukund Dewangan (2017): an LMV licence holder may drive transport vehicles of LMV class (GVW not exceeding 7,500 kg), so insurers cannot repudiate on this ground alone.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Section 164B of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides for:
o: Constitution of the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund for compulsory insurance cover to all road users, golden hour treatment and hit-and-run compensation
e: Section 164B creates the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund, financed by levies and grants, to support cashless 'golden hour' treatment, hit-and-run compensation and cover for all road users.

t: As per the IDV depreciation schedule, a vehicle aged more than 2 years but not more than 3 years attracts depreciation of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The schedule is: up to 6 months 5%; 6 months to 1 year 15%; 1 to 2 years 20%; 2 to 3 years 30%; 3 to 4 years 40%; 4 to 5 years 50%. Beyond 5 years IDV is fixed by mutual agreement.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the 2022 third party premium notification, the annual TP premium for a private car with engine capacity between 1000 cc and 1500 cc is:
e: The notified rates are ₹2,094 for cars below 1000 cc, ₹3,416 for 1000–1500 cc and ₹7,897 for cars exceeding 1500 cc. ₹1,366 is the rate for two-wheelers of 150–350 cc.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Which of the following is a 'transport vehicle' under Section 2(47) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?
o: A two-wheeler used by the owner
A public service vehicle, goods carriage, educational institution bus or private service vehicle
e: Transport vehicles include public service vehicles, goods carriages, educational institution buses and private service vehicles; they require permits, fitness certificates and attract different insurance rating.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: For an e-rickshaw insured as a passenger carrying vehicle, which statement is correct?
o: No third party cover is required as it is battery operated
It can only be insured under a private car policy
It is covered under the owner's two-wheeler policy
It requires compulsory third party cover like any motor vehicle used in a public place
e: E-rickshaws are motor vehicles under the Act (specifically recognised in 2015) and must have Chapter XI cover; TP premium for them is separately notified in the annual rate schedule.

t: An insured restricts his private car's third party property damage cover to the statutory minimum of ₹6,000. The discount allowed on the TP premium is:
e: Restriction of TPPD to ₹6,000 attracts a discount of ₹100 for private cars and commercial vehicles and ₹50 for two-wheelers on the liability premium.

t: An insured cancels his annual package policy after 7 months at his own request. The OD premium of ₹24,000 is refunded to the extent of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). On cancellation at the insured's request the insurer retains premium on short period scale, which is 80% for a period of 7 months. Refund = 20% of ₹24,000 = ₹4,800; had the insurer cancelled, pro-rata refund of 5/12 would apply.

t: A commercial goods carrying vehicle is rated for own damage premium on the basis of:
o: Gross vehicle weight (GVW), IDV, age and zone
e: Goods carriers are rated on GVW bands and IDV along with age and zone; passenger carriers are rated on seating/licensed carrying capacity.

t: An insured has accumulated 45% NCB. He makes a claim during the year. At renewal his NCB will be:
e: Any OD claim during the policy period wipes out the entire accumulated NCB at the next renewal (unless an NCB protection add-on applies); it does not merely step down.

t: The depreciation for arriving at IDV of a vehicle not exceeding 6 months of age is:
e: The IDV schedule starts at 5% for vehicles up to 6 months old, 15% from 6 months to 1 year, 20% for 1–2 years, 30% for 2–3 years, 40% for 3–4 years and 50% for 4–5 years.

t: The additional premium charged for a vehicle fitted with a fibre glass fuel tank is:
e: A flat additional premium of ₹50 is charged for vehicles fitted with fibre glass fuel tanks under the standard rating rules.

t: A two-wheeler owner opts for a voluntary deductible of ₹1,500. The discount on OD premium is:
e: Two-wheeler voluntary deductible discounts: ₹500 – 5% (max ₹50); ₹750 – 10% (max ₹75); ₹1,000 – 15% (max ₹125); ₹1,500 – 20% (max ₹200).

t: An NRI returning to India produces evidence of 3 claim-free years on his car abroad. Which statement is correct?
o: NCB earned abroad may be allowed on the Indian policy on production of proof, provided the Indian policy is taken within 3 years of expiry of the foreign policy
Foreign NCB cannot be recognised in India
NCB is allowed only if the same car is imported
e: Rating rules permit NCB earned on a vehicle abroad to be granted on an Indian policy, subject to documentary evidence and the time limit for the break between the two policies.

t: Under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, the certificate of insurance for a motor vehicle is issued in:
e: Rule 141 prescribes Form 51 for the certificate of insurance and Rule 142 prescribes Form 52 for a cover note. Forms 29/30 relate to transfer of ownership and Form 35 to termination of hypothecation.

t: Under the compulsory PA cover for owner-driver, no compensation is payable for death or injury:
o: Occurring while the vehicle is being towed
Directly or indirectly caused by intentional self-injury, suicide, or while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
e: The PA section excludes intentional self-injury, suicide or attempted suicide, physical defect or infirmity, and accidents occurring while under the influence of liquor or drugs.

t: Which of the following statements about the 'Schedule' of a motor policy is INCORRECT?
o: It states the IDV of the vehicle
It specifies the limitations as to use and the drivers clause
It contains the depreciation table for claims
It sets out the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal
e: The Schedule records the insured, vehicle particulars, IDV, period, premium, limitations as to use and drivers' clause, and the policy also contains the depreciation schedule for partial losses. Tribunal awards are not part of the policy.

t: The 'No admission of liability' condition in the motor policy means that:
o: The insured must not admit liability, make any offer or promise of payment without the insurer's written consent
The insurer never admits any claim
The insured cannot file a claim with MACT
The insurer must admit liability within 30 days
e: The insured must leave the handling of third party claims to the insurer, which has the right to conduct the defence or settlement in the insured's name; unauthorised admissions can prejudice the insurer.

t: A liability-only policy may be cancelled by the insured only in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever the insured wishes, with 7 days' notice
Only after a claim has been paid
Only on proof that the vehicle has been insured elsewhere, or has been sold/transferred, or is no longer in use (e.g. scrapped or registration cancelled)
e: Since TP cover is statutory, it cannot be cancelled merely at the insured's request; the insurer must be satisfied that double insurance exists, the vehicle is transferred, or it can no longer be used in a public place.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Which of the following is NOT a section of the standard Private Car Package Policy?
o: Section IV – Loss of personal belongings of passengers
Section I – Loss of or damage to the vehicle insured
Section II – Liability to third parties
Section III – Personal accident cover for owner-driver
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The package policy has three sections: own damage, third party liability and personal accident to owner-driver. Personal belongings cover is not a standard section, though it may be offered as an add-on.

t: Under the depreciation schedule for partial losses, metal parts of a vehicle aged between 1 and 2 years attract depreciation of:
e: The age-based schedule for 'all other parts' is: up to 6 months nil; 6 months–1 year 5%; 1–2 years 10%; 2–3 years 15%; 3–4 years 25%; 4–5 years 35%; 5–10 years 40%; above 10 years 50%.

t: The purpose of a 're-inspection' by the surveyor after repairs is to:
o: Confirm that the repairs assessed have actually been carried out and the replaced parts fitted before releasing payment
Fix the IDV for the next policy
e: Re-inspection verifies that the assessed repairs and replacements were completed, deterring inflated bills and claims for parts never replaced.

t: The maximum liability of the insurer under Section I (own damage) for any one loss is:
o: The repair cost without any limit
The invoice value of the vehicle
The IDV of the vehicle (plus IDV of declared accessories) less deductibles
e: The sum insured under a motor policy is the IDV, which is the ceiling for any OD claim; add-ons like Return to Invoice are needed to recover more than IDV.

t: A stolen two-wheeler was settled as a total loss at IDV ₹60,000 and ownership transferred to the insurer. Six months later the police recover the vehicle. The vehicle now:
o: Belongs to the insurer, which may dispose of it as salvage
Must be returned to the insured free of cost
Must be sold and proceeds shared equally
e: After a total loss settlement with subrogation and transfer of RC, the recovered vehicle is the insurer's property; the insured has already been indemnified.

t: A two-wheeler damaged in an accident is towed to the nearest garage at a cost of ₹600. The amount payable under the standard policy towards towing is:
e: The two-wheeler package policy limits reasonable removal and re-delivery charges to ₹300 (private cars ₹1,500, commercial vehicles ₹2,500) unless an enhanced towing add-on is purchased.

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits:
o: Payment of any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to buy insurance
Issue of a policy without a medical examination
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 41 bars rebating; contravention attracts a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh.

t: Ravi's 2-year-old car suffers accident damage: two tyres ₹16,000, plastic bumper ₹6,000, labour ₹4,000; the car body was also damaged. Compulsory deductible ₹1,000. The payable amount for these items is:
e: Tyres damaged along with the vehicle are paid at 50%: ₹8,000; plastic bumper at 50% depreciation: ₹3,000; labour ₹4,000. Total ₹15,000 less deductible ₹1,000 = ₹14,000.

t: Under the 2024 IRDAI master circular on general insurance, which of the following is correct regarding claim documentation?
o: Insurers may call for documents repeatedly until satisfied
Documents must be submitted within 24 hours
Insurers must not reject a claim for want of documents and should collect required documents at the time of policy issuance where possible, calling for only claim-related documents
e: The master circular directs that claims should not be rejected merely for non-submission of documents; insurers must seek only documents relevant to the claim and follow a clear, time-bound process.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Section 166(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, who among the following may NOT file an application for compensation?
o: The person who sustained the injury
The owner of the property damaged
The legal representatives of the deceased
e: Section 166 permits the injured person, owner of damaged property, legal representatives of the deceased, or an agent authorised by them to apply. The insurer is a respondent, not a claimant.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Suresh, aged 45, self-employed with established income of ₹20,000 per month, dies leaving a wife, three children and his mother (5 dependants). Using Pranay Sethi and Sarla Verma, the loss of dependency is:
e: Annual income ₹2,40,000 + 25% future prospects (self-employed, 40–50 years) = ₹3,00,000; deduct one-fourth (4–6 dependants) = ₹2,25,000; multiplier for age 41–45 is 14; ₹2,25,000 × 14 = ₹31,50,000.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: In Ningamma v. Chikkaiah (2009), the Supreme Court held that a person who borrows a vehicle and dies while driving it:
o: Steps into the shoes of the owner and cannot claim as a third party against the owner's insurer
Is a third party entitled to compensation under Section 166
Is covered under the hit-and-run scheme
e: The borrower is treated as the owner for the purposes of the policy; his legal heirs cannot claim against the insurer under the third party section since there is no tortfeasor other than the deceased himself.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Section 169 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Claims Tribunal:
o: Must follow the Code of Civil Procedure strictly
Has no power to summon witnesses
May follow summary procedure and has the powers of a civil court for taking evidence on oath and enforcing attendance of witnesses
Can only award compensation up to ₹5 lakh
e: Section 169 allows the Tribunal to follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit, while vesting it with civil court powers for evidence, witnesses and documents; there is no ceiling on the award.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under the amended Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, on receipt of the accident information report the insurer must designate an officer to settle the claim and make an offer within:
e: Section 149 (as substituted in 2019) requires the insurer's designated officer to make an offer of settlement within 30 days; if accepted, the Tribunal records it and payment follows, failing which the claim proceeds on merits.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Which of the following statements about the Sarla Verma multiplier for a deceased aged 58 years is correct?
e: The multiplier for the 56–60 age band is 9; it is 11 for 51–55, 7 for 61–65 and 5 for those above 65.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: A claimant accepts compensation of ₹5 lakh under Section 164 (no-fault). Can he subsequently file a claim under Section 166 for a higher amount from the same accident?
o: No; under Section 164(3)-(4), a person who accepts Section 164 compensation cannot pursue a fault-based claim for the same accident
Yes, but only for medical expenses
e: Section 164 requires the claimant to elect between the no-fault structured compensation and a fault-based claim under Section 166; accepting one bars the other for the same accident.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: The 'Key Replacement' add-on covers:
o: Replacement of lost or stolen vehicle keys and, where required, the lock set
Replacement of the ignition system after an accident
e: Key replacement pays for new keys and lock sets when keys are lost, stolen or damaged, subject to conditions such as an FIR for theft and limits on number of claims.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: In June 2022 IRDAI moved general insurance products, including motor own damage add-ons, to which product-approval approach?
o: Prior approval of every product by IRDAI
Approval by the General Insurance Council
Use and File, allowing insurers to launch products after board approval and file them with IRDAI
e: The 'Use and File' procedure replaced 'File and Use' for health and most general insurance products, speeding up launch of innovative motor add-ons such as telematics-based covers.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: A 'Daily Allowance' (loss of use) add-on provides:
o: A fixed daily amount for alternative transport while the insured vehicle is under accidental repair, for a specified number of days
e: The add-on compensates for loss of use by paying a fixed daily sum (typically for a limited number of days after a waiting period) while the vehicle is at the garage following an admitted OD claim.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, a complaint can be made to the Ombudsman within what period from the date of the insurer's final reply or rejection?
e: The complainant must first write to the insurer; if there is no reply within 30 days or the reply is unsatisfactory, a complaint can be lodged with the Ombudsman within one year, provided the matter is not pending before any court or consumer forum.

t: IRDAI's Insurance Fraud Monitoring Framework (2013) requires every insurer to:
o: Have a board-approved anti-fraud policy, a fraud monitoring function and report fraud statistics to IRDAI
e: The framework mandates an anti-fraud policy covering policyholder, intermediary and internal fraud, with processes for detection, investigation, reporting and employee awareness.

t: Which technology is commonly used by Indian insurers to speed up small own damage claims through self-inspection?
o: Mobile app based photo/video survey with AI-assisted damage estimation
e: Insurers use app-based self-survey where the customer uploads photos/videos; AI models estimate damage and cost, enabling quick settlement of low-value claims without a physical surveyor.
